projects.name: Customer Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
Build an internal analytics dashboard unifying two data sources behind interactive visualizations.

Scope:
1. Customer CSV processing — ingest raw CSV exports, validate schema, clean/normalize records, derive customer metrics (cohorts, retention, revenue aggregates).
2. Application log analysis — ingest app logs, parse and normalize events, derive error rates, latency and usage KPIs.
3. Visualization layer — dashboard UI with reusable chart components, filter/drill-down interactions, and a data-access layer over both pipelines.

Approach: five milestones (foundation -> CSV pipeline -> log pipeline -> visualization -> integration/deploy), with the two pipelines running in parallel. Every task is decomposed to complexity <= 6.

Success criteria: pipelines run reliably on schedules with error handling; dashboard renders both domains with working filters; end-to-end tests pass on fixtures; deployment and runbook documented.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, visualization, logs

tasks.name: M1 — Project Foundation & Data Contracts
tasks.details:
Establish the technical foundation both data pipelines and the dashboard will build on.

Deliverables:
- Repository structure, tooling, linting, CI scaffolding.
- Canonical data model and schema contracts shared by CSV ingestion, log ingestion, and the visualization layer.
- Local dev environment plus representative sample fixtures for CSV and logs.

Purpose: prevents rework when the two pipelines and the UI are developed in parallel. This milestone is the only true blocker at the project level.

tasks.name: M2 — Customer CSV Processing Pipeline
tasks.details:
Ingest customer CSV exports and turn them into clean, query-ready customer metrics.

Deliverables:
- CSV ingestion with schema validation and reject handling.
- Cleaning, normalization and deduplication of customer records.
- Customer aggregate metrics (cohorts, retention, revenue aggregates).
- Scheduled batch load job with retry, error routing and observability.

Runs in parallel with M3 once M1 data contracts are agreed.

tasks.name: M3 — Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
Ingest application logs and derive operational KPIs for the dashboard.

Deliverables:
- Log ingestion and parsing (structured, plain text, multiline stack traces, rotated files).
- Field extraction and normalization to the shared event schema.
- Error and event aggregation producing error rates, latency and usage KPIs.
- Scheduling, retry and dead-letter handling for the log pipeline.

Runs in parallel with M2 once M1 data contracts are agreed.

tasks.name: M4 — Visualization Components & Dashboard UI
tasks.details:
Build the dashboard shell, reusable chart components and the data-access layer.

Deliverables:
- Dashboard layout and design-system/component library setup.
- Customer metric visualizations (cohort, retention, revenue).
- Log and error visualizations (error-rate trends, event timeline).
- Data-access layer connecting the UI to both pipelines' outputs.
- Global filters, date ranges and drill-down interactions.

Consumes the outputs of M2 and M3, so component work is sequenced behind the relevant pipeline subtasks.

tasks.name: M5 — Integration, Testing & Deployment
tasks.details:
Prove the whole system works together and ship it.

Deliverables:
- End-to-end integration test across both pipelines and the dashboard, using sample fixtures.
- Performance and load validation of dashboard queries.
- Deployment pipeline and environment configuration.
- Documentation, operational runbook and handover.

Final milestone; depends on the completed data pipelines and visualization layer.

tasks.name: 1.1 Repository structure, tooling & CI scaffolding
tasks.details:
Set up the skeleton every later task builds on.

Work:
- Create repository/module layout (ingestion, transforms, metrics, api, ui).
- Configure linting, formatting, type checking, pre-commit hooks.
- Add CI workflow running lint + tests on every push.
- Add contribution conventions (branch naming, PR template).

Acceptance criteria:
- Fresh clone can run `install`, `lint` and `test` locally.
- CI runs green on an empty baseline commit.

tasks.name: 1.2 Canonical data model & schema contracts
tasks.details:
Define the single source of truth for data shapes so the CSV pipeline, log pipeline and UI can be built in parallel without rework.

Work:
- Document the customer record model (field names, types, nullability, PII classification).
- Document the normalized event/log record model and the shared metric/KPI result shape.
- Define the schema contract artefact the UI queries (metric name, dimensions, time grain).
- Agree versioning strategy for contract changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Written contract reviewed and signed off by pipeline and UI owners.
- Validation schemas exist in code and are importable by all three layers.
- A first contract version is committed and referenced from the project README.

tasks.name: 1.3 Local dev environment & sample data fixtures
tasks.details:
Give the team realistic data to develop and test against.

Work:
- Assemble anonymized customer CSV fixtures covering edge cases (blank fields, duplicate customers, odd date formats, non-UTF8 characters).
- Assemble application log fixtures covering structured JSON lines, plain text, multiline stack traces and a rotated file.
- Script a one-command local environment start (containers or local services).
- Document how to refresh fixtures.

Acceptance criteria:
- One command brings up the local environment.
- Fixtures load through a stub reader without manual editing.
- Edge-case fixtures are labelled so tests can target them.

tasks.name: 2.1 CSV ingestion & schema validation
tasks.details:
Get raw CSV files in and reject bad data loudly instead of silently.

Work:
- Implement a file reader handling encodings, delimiters and header variants.
- Validate every row against the 1.2 customer schema contract.
- Route invalid rows to a rejects table/file with a reason code per row.
- Emit ingestion counts (read, accepted, rejected) as structured logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Good fixture loads with 100% acceptance.
- Corrupt fixture produces reject reasons and does not crash the job.
- Ingestion counts are visible in logs and asserted by unit tests.

tasks.name: 2.2 Cleaning, normalization & deduplication
tasks.details:
Make accepted rows trustworthy and comparable.

Work:
- Normalize dates/timestamps to a single timezone and format.
- Normalize country/region, currency and categorical values against lookup lists.
- Trim and standardize text fields; mask or hash PII per the 1.2 classification.
- Deduplicate customers using a deterministic match key, keeping the most recent record.

Acceptance criteria:
- Edge-case fixture produces identical output across two consecutive runs (idempotent).
- Duplicate customers collapse to one canonical record.
- Unit tests cover each normalization rule.

tasks.name: 2.3 Customer metrics & aggregation logic
tasks.details:
Turn clean customer records into the numbers the dashboard will display.

Work:
- Compute customer counts, new vs returning, and active/inactive by period.
- Compute retention/cohort matrices by signup period.
- Compute revenue aggregates (total, per customer, per period) where revenue fields exist.
- Publish results in the shared metric result shape from 1.2.

Acceptance criteria:
- Metric outputs reconcile against hand-calculated values on the fixture set.
- Cohort matrix is correct at month boundaries.
- Metric tests run in CI with fixed expectations.

tasks.name: 2.4 Scheduled batch load, retries & observability
tasks.details:
Run the CSV pipeline unattended and safely.

Work:
- Schedule the batch job (configurable cadence, manual trigger).
- Add retry with backoff for transient failures.
- Add failure alerting and a job-status record per run.
- Ensure re-runs are idempotent and partially-failed runs are resumable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Job completes on schedule against fixtures with no manual step.
- Induced failure retries then alerts with a clear reason.
- Re-running a completed window does not double-count metrics.

tasks.name: 3.1 Log ingestion & multi-format parsing
tasks.details:
Read application logs of several shapes without losing lines.

Work:
- Ingest from file directories and rotated archives, tracking read offsets to avoid re-reading.
- Parse structured JSON lines and plain-text lines with a configurable pattern set.
- Handle multiline entries (stack traces) by joining continuation lines to their parent event.
- Route unparseable lines to a quarantine stream with the raw line preserved.

Acceptance criteria:
- All log fixtures parse with expected event counts.
- Multiline stack traces reconstruct as a single event.
- Offset tracking prevents duplicate ingestion across runs.

tasks.name: 3.2 Field extraction & normalization to event schema
tasks.details:
Convert heterogeneous log lines into the shared event schema.

Work:
- Extract timestamp, level/severity, service, request id, user id (hashed), route, status code, duration.
- Map severity strings onto a canonical level set.
- Normalize timestamps to UTC and handle clock-skew/skewed formats.
- Validate normalized events against the 1.2 event contract, quarantining failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- Extracted fields match expectations on every fixture type.
- Each parsed event validates against the shared contract.
- Malformed rows end up quarantined, not dropped silently.

tasks.name: 3.3 Error & event aggregation, KPI derivation
tasks.details:
Produce the operational numbers behind the log dashboards.

Work:
- Error rate per service/route over time with configurable time grain.
- p50/p95/p99 latency and request-volume trends.
- Top error signatures with counts, grouping stack traces by message fingerprint.
- Publish results in the shared metric result shape from 1.2.

Acceptance criteria:
- Error-rate and latency values reconcile with hand-computed fixture results.
- Fingerprinting groups identical stack traces together.
- Empty windows produce zero-filled series rather than gaps.

tasks.name: 3.4 Scheduling, retries & dead-letter handling
tasks.details:
Make the log pipeline dependable in production.

Work:
- Schedule ingestion and aggregation on a configurable cadence with manual trigger.
- Retry transient parse/storage failures with backoff.
- Route permanently failing records to a dead-letter store for inspection and replay.
- Emit per-run status, lag and record counts as metrics/alerts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline runs unattended against a growing log directory.
- Poison record lands in dead-letter without stalling the run.
- Dead-letter replay processes the record once the cause is fixed.

tasks.name: 4.1 Dashboard layout & component library setup
tasks.details:
Create the frame the charts live in.

Work:
- Dashboard shell: header, nav, page grid, responsive breakpoints.
- Theme tokens (color, spacing, typography) and a chart color palette that is accessible.
- Base chart wrapper component handling loading, empty and error states.
- Storybook or equivalent component gallery for review.

Acceptance criteria:
- Layout renders correctly at desktop, tablet and mobile widths.
- Base wrapper covers loading/empty/error states in the gallery.
- Palette passes a contrast check for key series colors.

tasks.name: 4.2 Customer metric visualization components
tasks.details:
Render the customer metrics from the CSV pipeline.

Work:
- KPI tiles: total customers, new customers, active customers.
- Retention/cohort heatmap driven by 2.3 output.
- Revenue trend chart and per-customer breakdown.
- Tooltips, legends and value formatting consistent across charts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each component renders real 2.3 fixture output, not mock data.
- Chart values match the underlying metric payload exactly.
- Components appear in the gallery with documented props.

tasks.name: 4.3 Log & error visualization components
tasks.details:
Render the operational metrics from the log pipeline.

Work:
- Error-rate over time chart with severity threshold bands.
- Event volume / request-rate timeline.
- Latency percentile chart (p50/p95/p99).
- Top error signatures table with counts and drill-through affordance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Components render real 3.3 fixture output.
- Percentile series are labelled and distinguish p50/p95/p99.
- Empty-window behaviour shows a zero series, not a broken chart.

tasks.name: 4.4 Dashboard data-access layer & API integration
tasks.details:
Give the UI a single, typed path to both pipelines' data.

Work:
- Define client-side query functions for each metric in the 1.2 contract.
- Implement request caching and cancellation for rapid filter changes.
- Standardize error surfacing and retry policy for failed queries.
- Type the responses from the shared schema contract.

Acceptance criteria:
- All chart components read through this layer, with no direct fetch calls in components.
- Types are generated/derived from the schema contract, not hand-copied.
- Failed query surfaces a retryable error state in the UI.

tasks.name: 4.5 Filters, date range & drill-down interactions
tasks.details:
Make the dashboard explorable rather than static.

Work:
- Global date-range selector with presets and custom range.
- Dimension filters (service, route, customer segment) reflected in the URL for shareable views.
- Drill-down from summary tiles into the matching detail charts.
- Loading/skeleton behaviour during filter transitions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Changing a filter updates every affected chart consistently.
- Reloading a URL restores the same filter state.
- Drill-down navigates to the correct filtered detail view.

tasks.name: 5.1 End-to-end integration test on sample fixtures
tasks.details:
Prove the three layers work together on real fixture data.

Work:
- Seed the CSV and log pipelines with the 1.3 fixtures.
- Run the pipelines end to end into the dashboard's data source.
- Verify each dashboard panel against expected fixture values.
- Automate the run in CI as a single end-to-end suite.

Acceptance criteria:
- One command runs pipelines + dashboard assertions from a clean environment.
- All panels pass their expected-value assertions.
- CI runs the end-to-end suite on every pull request.

tasks.name: 5.2 Performance & load validation
tasks.details:
Confirm the dashboard stays responsive at realistic data volumes.

Work:
- Generate a synthetic dataset at expected production scale (customers and log events).
- Measure dashboard query and panel render times, set a target (e.g. dashboard interactive under 3s).
- Identify and index/optimize the slowest queries.
- Record results as a baseline for future regression checks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented latency numbers for each panel at production scale.
- Every panel meets the agreed latency target, or has a filed follow-up.
- Baseline is checked into the repo for comparison.

tasks.name: 5.3 Deployment pipeline & environment configuration
tasks.details:
Ship the dashboard and both pipelines repeatably.

Work:
- Define environment configuration/secrets handling for staging and production.
- Build the deploy pipeline for the dashboard app and the two pipeline jobs.
- Add smoke checks post-deploy and an automatic rollback path.
- Document the release process and required approvals.

Acceptance criteria:
- One merge to main deploys to staging automatically.
- Production deploy requires approval and runs smoke checks.
- Rollback to the prior version is documented and rehearsed once.

tasks.name: 5.4 Documentation, runbook & handover
tasks.details:
Leave the team able to run and extend this without the build team.

Work:
- README covering architecture, local setup and how to add a new metric/chart.
- Operational runbook: schedules, alert meanings, dead-letter replay, re-run procedure.
- Metric dictionary documenting every KPI and its definition.
- Handover walkthrough session with the owning team.

Acceptance criteria:
- A new engineer can run the stack locally using only the README.
- Metric dictionary covers every panel on the dashboard.
- Handover session completed and recorded.
